title: Signed PPO clipping
prompt: Implement `ppo_loss(ratio, advantage, epsilon=.2)`. Example: ratio 1.5, advantage 2 gives -2.4.
tests:
assert abs(ppo_loss(1.5,2)+2.4)<1e-9, 'Cap positive-advantage improvement'
assert ppo_loss(1.5,-2)==3, 'Do not hide harmful probability increases'
assert abs(ppo_loss(.5,-2)-1.6)<1e-9, 'Cap improvement for a negative advantage'
assert ppo_loss(1,0)==0, 'Zero advantage gives zero policy loss'

title: Decouple stale data
prompt: Implement `decoupled_loss(behaviour, proximal, current, advantage, cap=2)`, epsilon .2. Example: .2,.3,.33,1 gives -1.65.
tests:
assert abs(decoupled_loss(.2,.3,.33,1)+1.65)<1e-9, 'Use proximal/behaviour times current/proximal objective'
assert abs(decoupled_loss(.01,.3,.6,1)+2.4)<1e-9, 'Cap importance weight at two and PPO ratio at 1.2'
assert abs(decoupled_loss(.2,.3,.6,-1)-3)<1e-9, 'Retain harmful movement for negative advantage'
hint: Cap only the importance ratio at cap; PPO uses its own interval.

title: Pre-step KL decision
prompt: Implement `should_stop(head_kls, threshold)`. None disables stopping; otherwise stop only when the sum exceeds the threshold. Example: [.01,.015], .02 gives True.
tests:
assert should_stop([.01,.015],.02), 'Summed head KL exceeds the limit'
assert not should_stop([.02],.02), 'Equality is not greater than'
assert not should_stop([9],None), 'None disables the stop'
hint: Check None before comparing the sum.
solution:
def should_stop(head_kls, threshold):
    return threshold is not None and sum(head_kls)>threshold
